text:
Ava: repro'd a stale-read during shard handoff. write acked on A, replication to B delayed, handoff flips ownership early, A still serves old slab entries.
Tom: timeline? sounds like ownership flipped before replication finished.
Ava: write -> ack A -> async replicate to B -> B gets takeover message -> becomes authoritative -> read routed to A returns old value because its slab hadn't applied the write and demote didn't prevent serving.
Chen: related to gen/TOCTOU but this needs lsn visibility across owners.
Maya: idea: token-based takeover. new owner requests takeover token from current owner, owner replies with token including min_lsn flushed. new owner waits until its applied_lsn >= token.min_lsn then flips authoritative bit. old owner marks handoff_in_progress and refuses to serve slab entries below token.min_lsn.
Tom: reading path simple check: if (handoff_in_progress && slab.lsn(key) < takeover_min_lsn) fallback_read(); else slab.read(). That only adds a cheap per-entry lsn compare.
Ava: token avoids synchronous replication in the fast path; if new owner already has lsn >= required we flip immediately. Otherwise wait up to N ms then force takeover and log forced-takeovers.
Chen: tests: synthetic high-write + frequent rebalance, chaos dropping replication. metrics: handoff.token_wait_ms, handoff.fallback_reads, handoff.forced_takeovers.
Maya: ops-bot create canary ticket.
ops-bot: created #CANARY-919: "handoff-token takeover canary" assigned to @ava, due 2026-04-10 :white_check_mark:
Ava: will spike and bench; default timeout 200ms, enable behind runtime.flags.handoff_token_takeover and a canary ring.
Tom: good compromise between safety and low-latency handoffs.
